# select_users (Data Source)

Lists the users of the organization. Use it to check that an email address belongs to a user before you grant a role to it.

## About

The data source lists all users of the organization, on all pages. The API has no filter, so the provider applies the `emails` filter after it gets the list. The filter compares email addresses without case.

An email address in `emails` that belongs to no user does not cause an error: it is not in `users`. A role grant works for an email address before that person signs in, so a missing user is not always a problem. To find the missing email addresses, compare `emails` with the email addresses in `users`, as in the example below. Use a `precondition` to stop the apply, or a `check` block to give a warning. The [user admin guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/get-select/select/latest/docs/guides/user-admin) shows a `check` block.

This data source is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/users`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# All users of the organization.
data "select_users" "all" {}

output "user_emails" {
  value = [for user in data.select_users.all.users : user.email]
}

# Only the users with these email addresses. The match ignores case. An email
# that belongs to no user is not an error: it is not in `users`.
locals {
  editor_emails = toset(["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com"])
}

data "select_users" "editors" {
  emails = local.editor_emails
}

locals {
  missing_editors = setsubtract(
    [for email in local.editor_emails : lower(email)],
    [for user in data.select_users.editors.users : lower(user.email)],
  )
}

# Stops the grant when the email is not a SELECT user yet. Without this
# precondition, SELECT accepts the grant, and it takes effect when the person
# first signs in.
resource "select_user_role" "editors" {
  for_each = local.editor_emails

  email = each.value
  role  = "editor"

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = !contains(local.missing_editors, lower(each.value))
      error_message = "${each.value} is not a SELECT user. Check the spelling, or ask the person to sign in first."
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `emails` (Set of String) The email addresses to find. The match ignores case. If you omit it, the data source returns all users. An email address that belongs to no user does not cause an error: it is not in `users`. An empty set returns no users.

### Read-Only

- `users` (Attributes List) The users that were found, sorted by email address. A person who has not signed in to SELECT yet can be absent from the list. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--users))

<a id="nestedatt--users"></a>
### Nested Schema for `users`

Read-Only:

- `email` (String) The user's email address, as SELECT stores it.
- `id` (String) The user's identifier in SELECT.
- `identity_provider` (String) The identity provider the user signs in through.
- `last_login_sso_groups` (List of String) The SSO groups the user belonged to at their most recent login. Null if SELECT has no record.
- `last_login_time` (String) When the user last signed in — RFC 3339 UTC. Null if SELECT has no record.
- `name` (String) The user's display name. Null if SELECT has none.
